race_name: The Millars UCI Gran Fondo World Series

top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at The Millars UCI Gran Fondo World Series. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 97 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic The Millars UCI Gran Fondo World Series' demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.
75ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At The Millars UCI Gran Fondo World Series, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of The Millars UCI Gran Fondo World Series. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 97, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
7,254ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
7,254ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at The Millars UCI Gran Fondo World Series. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 97 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 7,254ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for The Millars UCI Gran Fondo World Series’s 97 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at The Millars UCI Gran Fondo World Series rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 97 miles of mixed terrain in Castellón de la Plana, Castellón Province, Spain.
